title: Proof pages for an accounting firm
metaTitle: Accounting firm case study page, with the decision
excerpt: An accounting firm case study page should show the constraint, the decision, and who the work was for. A dashboard without a decision is decoration.
alt: A long, quiet office corridor with glass rooms, a teal sofa, and a dark kitchen, a specific workplace rather than a skyline used as proof.
caption: A corridor, a sofa, and a kitchen, ordinary and identifiable. Photograph via Unsplash.

faqs.question: What should an accounting case study include?
faqs.answer: Include the constraint, the decision, and the kind of company, plus who did the work. Say what you refused to do, such as issuing a pack on a ledger you did not trust. End with how a similar founder can book a call and what they should have ready.

faqs.question: Can a firm publish a client's financial results?
faqs.answer: Only with a clear right to do so, and rarely with the figures themselves. Remove names and numbers that would identify the company. Do not invent a growth statistic or write the client's quote yourself. If a detail is necessary and identifying, leave it out.

faqs.question: Are dashboard screenshots useful?
faqs.answer: They are useful when they show a decision, such as a checkpoint list before you call a month closed, built from dummy data and captioned as a sample. A cropped chart with no sentence is decoration. Skip the image if you cannot make it without leaking a file.

sources.title: How Long Do Users Stay on Web Pages?

markdown:
An accounting firm case study page should show the constraint, the decision, and who did the work for what kind of company. Screenshots of a dashboard, with no decision attached, are decoration. End on how a similar founder can book a call. A founder who needs a calm expert is looking for evidence that you have seen a year like theirs and that a person made a judgment, not that you own a chart template.

You usually cannot publish the client's numbers. Revenue, margins, and a lender's name will identify them or betray a confidence. The proof has to live in the constraint and the decision. Google's helpful-content guidance asks you to show how work was done, and it treats trust as central on topics that affect financial stability. A proof page about books is that kind of page. A borrowed growth percentage is the opposite of trust.

## Constraint, decision, and the kind of company

Write those three near the top, in sentences a stranger can repeat.

The constraint is what made the year hard. Eight months of unreconciled accounts before a raise. A clinic whose practitioner billings lived in one system and whose bills lived in another. A shop that had stock in the back room and a different stock figure in the ledger. A founder who had been the bookkeeper until the product needed them full time. The constraint is why the work was not a routine close. Without it, "we improved the numbers" sounds like advertising.

The decision is what you chose, and what you refused. You split the work into a paid look, then a cleanup to a named date, then a monthly close. You told them the lender pack could not be built until the cleanup finished. You refused to forecast a round on top of a ledger you did not believe. You moved payroll out of the monthly fee because it was a different job. The decision is the proof that someone thought. A page that only says "successful engagement" hides the thinking the next founder hopes to hire.

The kind of company is the sort. Owner-led studio. Independent clinic. Shop with inventory. Product company before a first finance hire. That label is how the next founder recognizes themselves. Name who did the work, by role if not by a face, so the page still answers who and for whom. If that person has left, update the page or retire it.

Keep each of those tight. Nielsen Norman Group found that people read only about a quarter of the text on pages they open, and often leave within 10 to 20 seconds. The three facts have to survive the skim.

## What you can show when the numbers are private

Assume the figures are confidential. Design the page around that, instead of blurring a screenshot and hoping.

Remove names, exact revenues, investor names, and any figure that would let a competitor or an employee guess the company. Say that you have changed identifying details. The reader should understand this is a pattern. If a detail is necessary and identifying, drop the detail or drop the page.

Do not write the client's praise and sign it with their industry. A quotation you authored is a fiction. If they approved a specific sentence in writing, use that sentence alone. Most firms will not have one. The page can still be useful.

What you can show is your method. The order you opened the ledger. The checkpoint where you stopped and repriced. The report you refused to issue. The shape of the fee for the phase. Those are yours. They teach the next founder what the relationship feels like, which is the calm they came to check.

The Princeton GEO paper, from Aggarwal and colleagues, reported that citations, quotations, and statistics raised source visibility, with their methods boosting visibility by more than 40 percent on the queries they tested. That is not a reason to invent a statistic about a client. "Revenue up 30 percent" with no basis is worse than silence. If you have no figure you are allowed to publish, describe the decision and stop.

Public work follows a different rule. A store such as Down the Cove can show the shop because the shop is public. A founder's ledger is not a shop window. Do not treat a management pack as if it were a homepage.

## Screenshots are evidence or they are furniture

A screenshot earns its place when it shows the decision. A checklist of the reconciliations you required before a close, with the client name removed. A staged pack built from dummy data, captioned as an example of the format, not as their results. A simple diagram of the phases: look, cleanup, monthly close.

A screenshot of a beautiful chart with the axis cropped, a skyline, or a laptop in a cafe shows nothing about the judgment. Dashboards without a sentence are how firms perform competence. The sentence is the competence.

Caption the image with the decision it supports. "The checkpoint list we used before we would call a month closed. Sample layout, not a client file." Alt text describes the picture. It should not be a string of service keywords, and it should not claim a result the image does not contain.

If you cannot produce even a staged example without leaking a file, skip the image. A clear paragraph is better than a risky blur. Ask the person who did the work to read the draft and point at anything that still identifies the company. Do this before the page is public.

## How long, and what to leave out

One pattern, one decision. Three victories on one page teach none of them. If you have three patterns you can tell, publish three pages. Each ends on a booking for a similar founder.

A useful length is the length of the decision. The constraint. What you looked at first. What you recommended. What the founder still had to decide, because you do not run their company. What a similar founder should have ready if they want the same kind of help.

Leave out the skyline, the awards, and an essay on the importance of compliance. Those are other pages, or they are cuts. A founder who wanted a textbook is not booking a fit call. A founder who wants to know if you are steady will read the decision and look for the button.

Link to the service this proof supports and to the person who did the work if they are still there. Label the page in the menu by the job, not by the words case study, if your founders do not say that phrase. "Cleanup before a raise" is a label. "Insights" is a drawer.

Do not include a before-and-after of their cash if you cannot show the numbers honestly. A decorative arrow pointing up is a small version of the invented statistic. Calm firms do not need it.

## End on a call a similar founder can book

The last section is practical. If your year looks like this, book a call. Know your entity, your ledger, and the question. Bring last year's return if you have it. You do not need a perfect pack to earn the conversation.

Say what the call will not do. It will not be a completed cleanup, and it will not be a tax opinion delivered in the booking confirmation. It will tell them whether this kind of company and this kind of constraint are ones you take, and what the first phase looks like. That matches the care the page just described. A proof page about refusing a sloppy forecast should not end with "get an instant quote."

Repeat the boundary. If this pattern was for a studio with project invoices, say whether a shop with heavy stock would be a different job or a job you do not take. The right founder feels found. The wrong one is spared a wasted month.

Only invite work you still do. A proof page for a service you retired is a trap. Take it out of the menu or mark it as a past pattern.

## A test before you publish

Hand the draft to someone who does not know the file. Ask them to name the constraint, the decision, and the kind of company. If they cannot, the page is still a mood. Ask what they would bring to a call if their year rhymed with this one. If they cannot, the ending is too soft.

Then ask a colleague who was not on the work whether anything identifies the client. Cut that detail. It is easier than a phone call after a founder recognizes their own margin on your site.

Read it once for costume. Skyline, excellence, and a stock city do not make a decision more credible. Plain sentences do. If the only proof you have is the adjective, you do not have a proof page yet. Wait until you have a decision you can tell.

## Where the page sits

The proof page is not the navigation. A founder who believes the decision still has to find the job, in words they already use, and one path should book a call. Read [how to build the navigation as a map of jobs](/blog/navigation-for-an-accounting-firm) before you file this page under a menu called resources.

When you want help shaping a proof page that stays specific without exposing a client, look at [Hanabi's services](https://tryhanabi.com/#services). Bring one constraint and the decision you actually made.
